title: Lecture 1 — Languages PDF Exam
subject: Programming Languages
description: 20 unique Lecture 1 questions adapted from the uploaded quiz/midterm collection. Grammar and variable-binding questions are outside the confirmed Lecture 1 scope and are omitted. Correct answers follow visible source markings; explanations and three sets of missing choices were added for practice. The highlight is a study priority, not a confirmed prediction of the next exam.

questions.question: The ease with which programs can be read and understood is:
questions.explanation: Readability concerns how easily people understand a program. The PDF marks Readability.

questions.question: A language implementation method that does not translate the entire program into machine code, and generally has slower execution, is:
questions.explanation: The PDF marks Interpretation. Pure interpretation executes through an interpreter rather than first producing a complete machine-code program.

questions.question: Exception handling and type checking increase which language evaluation criterion?
questions.explanation: Type checking detects type errors; exception handling supports responses to exceptional conditions. The PDF marks Reliability.

questions.question: The process of collecting system program units and linking them to a user program is called:
questions.explanation: The source calls this Linking and loading: needed program units are combined with the user program to prepare execution.

questions.question: A collection of tools used in software development is called:
questions.explanation: A programming environment is a collection of development tools, rather than just one compiler or interpreter.

questions.question: Which language category became dominant under the influence of von Neumann computer architecture?
questions.explanation: Imperative variables, assignments and iteration closely match the memory and execution model of von Neumann architecture.

questions.question: The ease with which programs can be moved from one implementation to another is:
questions.explanation: Portability concerns moving a program between implementations or platforms.

questions.question: APL is highly expressive but difficult to read. Which design trade-off does this illustrate?
questions.explanation: Compact expressive notation can help writing while making reading harder. The graded screenshot marks Writability vs. readability; the earlier copy on page 6 has conflicting grading.

questions.question: The ease with which a language can be used to create programs is:
questions.explanation: Writability concerns the ease of expressing and creating programs.

questions.question: Programs produced by compilers generally execute faster than programs run through pure interpreters.
questions.explanation: The source marks True for its conventional compilation versus pure-interpretation comparison. This is about execution speed, not translation time; it is not a universal benchmark for every implementation.

questions.question: In the compilation model used by the source, which phase generates intermediate code?
questions.explanation: The PDF marks Semantic analysis. In this course model, semantic analysis and intermediate-code work precede machine-code generation.

questions.question: A relatively small set of primitive constructs, combined in a relatively small number of ways, improves which criterion?
questions.explanation: The source marks Readability. Overall simplicity and consistent feature combinations help readers understand programs.

questions.question: Which implementation method does the source describe as rarely used for traditional high-level languages?
questions.explanation: The PDF marks Pure interpreter. Treat this as the source's historical implementation comparison, rather than a claim about every modern language.

questions.question: Which tool handles directives that include code from other files before compilation?
questions.explanation: Preprocessing handles directives such as includes and macros before the main compilation stages.

questions.question: Which compilation phase transforms lexical units into parse trees?
questions.explanation: Syntax analysis organizes tokens into a grammatical structure such as a parse tree.

questions.question: Powerful C++ pointers allow access to hardware but can reduce reliability. Which trade-off is marked in the source?
questions.explanation: The source marks Writability vs. reliability. The Lecture 1 handout describes the same pointer example as flexibility versus reliability; this item preserves the PDF's terminology.

questions.question: Compilers are necessarily much faster than pure interpreters in the translation process.
questions.explanation: The PDF marks False. Translation time and program execution time are different comparisons; faster compiled execution does not imply this claim about translation time.

questions.question: Which implementation method translates programs into an intermediate language that is then executed by an interpreter?
questions.explanation: Hybrid implementation separates translation into an intermediate representation from execution by an interpreter. The source provides only the selected answer; the other choices were added for practice.

questions.question: Which implementation method translates programs into machine-language code before execution?
questions.explanation: A compiler translates source to machine code in the model used here. The source provides only the selected answer; the other choices were added for practice.

questions.question: Java array-index checks improve safety but increase execution time. Which trade-off does this illustrate?
questions.explanation: Bounds checks improve reliability while adding runtime work. The source provides only the selected answer; the other choices were added for practice.
